title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of Retrofit Emission Control devices (REC) for heavy duty vehicles, agricultural and forestry tractors and non-road mobile machinery equipped with compression ignition engines
scope_summary: Approves Retrofit Emission Control devices (REC) for particulate matter, NOx, or both. These devices are retrofitted to compression-ignition engines in M2, M3 and N vehicles (excluding vehicles approved to R83), in category T vehicles, and in variable- or constant-speed non-road mobile machinery with engines of more than 18 kW and up to 560 kW.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to Retrofit Emission Control devices (REC) to be installed: 2.1 On category M2, M3 and N vehicles and their CI engines, excluding those vehicles approved according to Regulation No. 83; 2.2 On CI engines having a net power higher than 18 kW but not more than 560 kW installed in non-road mobile machinery, operated under variable speed; 2.3 On CI engines having a net power higher than 18 kW but not more than 560 kW installed in non-road mobile machinery, operated under constant speed; 2.4 On CI engines having a net power higher than 18 kW but not more than 560 kW installed in category T vehicles.
vehicle_categories: Non-road mobile machinery (CI engines >18 kW to 560 kW, variable or constant speed)
applies_to_components: Particulate reduction REC (e.g. particulate filters, including regeneration system and strategy)
NOx reduction REC / DeNOx system (e.g. SCR, lean NOx catalysts, NOx absorbers)
Combined NOx and PM reduction REC
Sensors and software essential to REC operation
On-board operator warning system and operator inducement system
Reagent tank and dosing system (reagent-based REC)
Installation instructions and retrofit installation of REC
relation_to_other_regulations: Excludes vehicles approved according to UN Regulation No. 83 (light-duty emissions).
Refers to UN Regulation No. 49 for the engine family definition (para. 7), the ESC/ETC/WHSC/WHTC test cycles, PM and particle number definitions, and measurement procedures.
Refers to UN Regulation No. 96 for the engine family definition (para. 7), the NRSC/NRTC test cycles and the PM definition for non-road and tractor engines.
Refers to the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 for vehicle category definitions.
Annex 9 relates REC classes and reduction efficiencies to achieving the limits of the next more stringent emission stage (R49/R96 limits).

defined_terms.definition: Any particulate reduction system, NOx-reduction system or combination of both used for retrofit purposes, including essential sensors and software; systems that only modify existing engine controls are not REC.
A REC intended to control particulate matter emissions only that does not increase direct NO2 emissions.
A REC intended to control PM only that does not increase direct tailpipe NO2 emissions by more than the percentage specified in paragraph 8.4.2.
A REC intended to control NOx emissions only.
A REC intended to control both particulate matter and NOx emissions.
A REC whose particulate mass or particle number reduction efficiency qualifies it for a classification class, with the regeneration system and strategy forming part of it.
A family of particulate reduction systems that are technically identical in function according to paragraph 14.
A REC whose NOx mass emission reduction efficiency qualifies it for a classification class.
A family of NOx reduction systems that are technically identical in function according to paragraph 15.
An exhaust aftertreatment system designed to reduce NOx emissions, such as lean NOx catalysts, NOx absorbers and SCR systems.
A system of the REC capable of detecting NOx control malfunctions and identifying them via stored information and/or off-board communication.
A device that detects incorrect operation or removal of the REC.
The system that monitors the operation of emission control measures in the engine and/or REC system according to paragraph 18.
Any medium stored on-board in a tank and provided to the exhaust aftertreatment system on request of the emission control system.
External test equipment used for off-board communication with the NCD system.
A publicly available scan-tool capable of reading failure messages.
A scan-tool used only by the REC manufacturer and authorized dealers that reads failure messages and enables engine start after operator inducement.
Any additional measure to initiate regeneration on a periodic or continuously regenerating REC.
A regeneration process of an exhaust aftertreatment system occurring permanently or at least once per applicable test cycle.
A regeneration process occurring periodically, typically within less than 100 hours of normal engine operation, during which emission standards can be exceeded.
The range of engines to which an approved REC can be applied.
The emissions of an engine or engine system without any REC, i.e. engine-out emissions or the tailpipe emissions downstream of existing aftertreatment.
The engine, the emission control system and the communication interface between engine ECU(s) and other powertrain or vehicle control units.
A manufacturer's grouping of engine systems with similar exhaust emission characteristics per paragraph 7 of R49 or R96.
An engine selected from an engine family whose emission characteristics are representative of that family.
The ratio between emissions downstream of the REC and engine baseline emissions, calculated per paragraph 8.3.4.
A reduction efficiency in per cent that the REC must meet to be certified to a level specified in paragraph 8.3.
The person or body responsible for correct and safe installation of the approved REC.
The PM loading stored in a particulate reduction system, expressed as a proportion of its maximum loading before external regeneration.

applicability_hints: Applies only to retrofit (aftermarket) aftertreatment devices for CI (diesel) engines, not to original-equipment emission systems, which fall under R49/R96.
Software-only or calibration-only modifications of existing engine controls are explicitly not REC.
Sensors, software, regeneration systems and reagent dosing/tank hardware essential to REC operation are part of the REC approval.
Diesel particulate filters, oxidation catalyst + DPF combinations, and SCR/lean-NOx/NOx-absorber kits sold for retrofit fall under this regulation.
Light-duty vehicles approved to R83 are excluded; N1 vehicles are only covered if not approved under R83.
Non-road mobile machinery and tractor engines are covered only within the >18 kW to 560 kW net power range.
Reagent-based (e.g. urea SCR) retrofit systems trigger NCD, operator warning and inducement requirements (7.7, Annex 10).
Any REC affecting a vehicle with OBD needs marking/compatibility information (4.2(c)) and may fall under Annex 12.
Retrofit installers and owner/operator documentation are regulated through installation instructions (para. 20, Annex 11).
